title: Crumble the Corgi and the Wobbly Bridge
markdown:
It was a bright sunny morning, the kind where the sun tickles your nose like a playful puppy and the birds sing their happiest chirpiest tunes. Crumble the corgi, with his short stout legs and an even stouter sense of purpose, trotted along a sun-dappled path. Beside him, a flash of bushy tail and bright darting eyes, was Walnut the squirrel. They had a very special job: delivering a basket of the most delicious acorn muffins, still wonderfully warm from Mrs. Badger’s oven, to the little library tucked beside the very old oak tree. The library was for Elder Willow, a wise old tree who loved nothing more than a good story and a warm tasty muffin.

"Are we nearly there, Walnut?" Crumble puffed, short legs working with admirable speed, breath coming a little faster. "My tummy is rumbling for a muffin, but mostly for seeing Elder Willow smile."

"Almost, Crumble, almost," chirped Walnut. "Just a little further along the Whispering Stream path. It is the nicest route."

The Whispering Stream path was a lovely way to go. Smooth grey pebbles sang a little skitter-skatter tune. Little green ferns tickled their ankles like tiny giggling fingers. But it had one little obstacle. Right in the middle, where the stream chuckled and gurgled over smooth stones, lay a fallen log. To Walnut it was a rather simple and charming bridge. To Crumble it seemed to stretch on and on. It wobbled with every little ripple. Crumble had a secret. A little fluttery feeling, like a butterfly trapped in his tummy, whenever he looked at wobbly things. A quiet worry that sometimes made his usually steady paws feel a bit damp and his proud tail tuck just a tiny bit closer to his body.

They reached the stream. The log lay across it, looking quite innocent to Walnut, who could scamper across any surface with ease. Crumble stopped abruptly. His velvety ears drooped ever so slightly. His usually bright eyes looked a little uncertain. A tremor rippled through his sturdy short legs. "Oh, dear." The words caught in his throat like a tiny crumb. "It looks very wobbly." He felt a familiar strong urge to turn around, to find a different path, any path that did not involve such a precarious crossing. His paws felt stuck to the ground.

Walnut hopped onto a nearby sun-warmed stone. "It is just a log, Crumble. A strong sturdy log. And Elder Willow is waiting with such excitement for her birthday muffins. She is expecting them for her party this very afternoon. Think of her happy smile."

"But my paws." Crumble looked down at them as if they belonged to someone else. They felt clumsy and uncertain, like new shoes that did not quite fit.

He took a deep breath, a little huff of corgi air that puffed out his cheeks. He looked at Walnut, who gave him a slow reassuring nod, bushy tail giving a friendly twitch. Slowly, very slowly, Crumble placed one paw onto the log. It felt surprisingly firm, with a gentle spring. He took another step. And another. His heart thumped like a little drummer boy against his ribs, but he kept going. He focused on the soft mossy green of the log beneath his paws, on the gentle soothing murmur of the stream below, and most importantly on the image of Elder Willow’s happy wrinkled smile. Then, with a final brave little hop, he was on the other side. He had not tumbled. He had not wobbled uncontrollably. A tiny victory, but a big one for Crumble.

They continued, the path now feeling a little lighter. Soon they arrived at the little library, a cozy nook at the base of the grand old oak. The air smelled of sunshine, old paper, and something faintly sweet, like baked apples. Elder Willow, her ancient bark etched with a thousand kind wrinkles, smiled warmly. "Ah, my dear Crumble and Walnut. Come in, come in. I was just about to start a story about a brave little robin. Oh, where are my special birthday muffins?"

Crumble set the basket down with a triumphant little wag. But as Walnut began to arrange the muffins on a neat little leaf platter, he let out a small surprised gasp. "The dewdrop. The special sparkling dewdrop for Elder Willow’s morning tea. It is gone." He peered into the basket, shuffling through the remaining muffins. It was true. The tiny perfectly glistening droplet, carefully gathered from the finest morning petals, was missing. It was her very favourite thing to sip, and a very important part of her special birthday treat.

"Oh dear." Crumble’s ears drooped again, not from fear this time, but from concern. He remembered a patch of particularly tall dewy bluebells just before the wobbly bridge. And he remembered how that dewdrop, nestled on a velvety petal, had sparkled like a tiny diamond. He had to go back. And this time he had to go back alone.

"I will go." He surprised even himself with the steadiness of his voice. "I will get it."

Walnut’s bright eyes went wide. "Are you sure, Crumble? The bridge."

"I will be careful." He truly meant it. He trotted back to the stream, heart giving a little fluttery lurch as he saw the log again. He took a deep breath and stepped on. The rough wood felt slick with morning dew. The rushing water below made a louder more insistent sound, and the damp earthy smell of the stream filled his nose. His heart pounded. He remembered the feel of it beneath his paws, the gentle sway that was more like a friendly hello from the stream than a dangerous wobble. He found the tall bluebells, petals shimmering with tiny perfect drops. Carefully, oh so carefully, he scooped the most perfect largest dewdrop into a small sturdy leaf he carried, like a tiny cup.

With the precious dewdrop safely cradled, Crumble crossed the bridge again. He felt a little lighter, a little quicker this time. He met Walnut, who was waiting by the stream with a relieved sigh and a wide happy smile. Together they continued the short distance back to the library.

"Elder Willow." His voice was full of pride as he held out the leaf. "Your special dewdrop."

Elder Willow’s leaves rustled with what sounded like a gentle joyful sigh. "Oh, thank you, Crumble. You are such a thoughtful brave friend." She carefully sipped the dewdrop, a look of pure calm happiness on her ancient bark-covered face. Her leaves seemed to shimmer a little brighter.

Crumble watched her, and a feeling of warmth spread through him, far warmer and more satisfying than any acorn muffin. As they walked away from the oak, he saw a fallen leaf float down onto a puddle. For a moment he imagined the leaf wobbling on the water’s surface, then he simply watched it settle, his own paws steady on the path. He gave a happy little trot, tail held high.
